title: The Bank Levy (Definitions and Amendments) Regulations 2026

title: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations designate BlackRock Financial Management, Inc., Bloomberg L.P., Bottomline Technologies Limited, Broadridge Financial Solutions Limited and Form3 UK Limited as critical third parties. The Regulations amend the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/777) to add the entities to the list of designated critical third parties.

title: The Human Rights Act 1998 (Remedial) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the Human Rights Act 1998 (“the HRA”) to address a finding of the European Court of Human Rights of a breach of Article 13 of the European Convention on Human Rights (“the Convention”) in the case of S.W. v United Kingdom (Application no. 87/18).

title: The Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector and Social Rented Sector (England) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector and Social Rented Sector (England) Regulations 2020 (S.I. 2020/312) (“the Principal Regulations”).

title: The Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025 (S.I. 2025/1042) (“the 2025 Regulations”), also known as “Awaab’s Law”, which prescribe requirements with which a landlord of social housing is required to comply by virtue of the covenant implied by section 10A(2) of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 (c. 70).

title: The Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Act 2025 (Specified Purposes Related to Policing) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations specify purposes related to policing for the purposes of sections 30 to 34 of the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Act 2025 (c. 31) (“the 2025 Act”).

title: The Statement of Trade Union Rights Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make provision about the written statement which an employer is required to give to a worker under section 136A of the Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992 (“the 1992 Act”). Section 136A was inserted into the 1992 Act by section 58 of the Employment Rights Act 2025 (“the 2025 Act”).

The Parking Places (Disabled Persons’ Vehicles) (Amendment No. 5) Order (Northern Ireland) 2026
The Air Navigation (Restriction of Flying) (Preston, Lancashire) Regulations 2026
The Town and Country Planning (Fees for Applications, Deemed Applications, Requests and Site Visits) (England) (Amendment and Transitional Provision) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Town and Country Planning (Fees for Applications, Deemed Applications, Requests and Site Visits) (England) Regulations 2012 (S.I. 2012/2920) (“the 2012 Regulations”).

title: The Air Navigation (Restriction of Flying) (Helicopter Flight) (No. 10) Regulations 2026
The Service and Administration Charges (England) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make provision about service charges and administration charges in relation to leases of dwellings in England.

title: The Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003 Remedial Order 2026
summary: This Order principally amends the Mental Health Care and Treatment (Scotland) Act 2003 (“the 2003 Act”) to remove an incompatibility with the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). The ability of the Mental Health Tribunal for Scotland (“the Tribunal”) to specify and subsequently modify, “recorded matters” in a “civil” order such as a community treatment order but not in a “forensic” order such as a compulsion order was found to violate article 14 (protection from discrimination) of the ECHR in the case of X v Mental Health Tribunal for Scotland [2022] CSOH 78.

title: The Scotland Act 1998 (Agency Arrangements) (Specification) (Digital Waste Tracking) Order 2026
summary: This Order paves the way for the Scottish Ministers and a Minister of the Crown to enter into agency arrangements, under which a Minister of the Crown can exercise certain functions of the designated person acting under, or in accordance with, any regulations made under section 34CA of the Environmental Protection Act 1990. Any such arrangements would be agreed between Ministers of the Crown and the Scottish Ministers.

title: The Secretaries of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport and the Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster Order 2026
summary: This Order in Council is made under sections 1 and 2 of the Ministers of the Crown Act 1975 (c. 26).

title: The Collective Investment Schemes (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make an amendment to the Collective Investment Schemes (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/325) (“CIS Regulations”), regarding temporary recognition for the purposes of Part 17 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (c. 8).

title: The Building Insurance Information (England) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make provision regarding information about insurance that a landlord must give to a tenant where a service charge includes an amount payable for that insurance. They concern leases of dwellings in England.

title: The Feed-in Tariffs (Amendment) (British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme Excluded Electricity) Order 2026
summary: This Order is made in exercise of the powers in sections 43(3)(a) and 104(2) of the Energy Act 2008 (c. 32). It amends the Feed-in Tariffs Order 2012 (S.I. 2012/2782) to make amendments as to how annual levelisation payments are calculated under article 27 of that Order. In particular, this Order introduces an exemption from that calculation for electricity supplied to customers operating in certain manufacturing sectors, under the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme.

title: The Maximum Number of Judges (Scotland) Order 2026
summary: Article 2 of this Order amends section 1(1) of the Court of Session Act 1988 so as to increase the maximum number of persons who may be appointed as judges of the Court of Session from 36 to 40. Article 3 revokes the Maximum Number of Judges (Scotland) Order 2022 which had previously increased the maximum number of judges of the Court of Session to 36.
